$comment: THE ONE DECLARED KUBERNETES VERSION. Every tool that renders or validates a
manifest against a Kubernetes API surface reads it from here.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-09-01 the tree carried THREE separate literals and
TWO different answers, neither of which was what the cluster runs:
src/Core.TypeScript/hygiene/audit-observability-chain.ts   1.31.0
the legacy tree's manifest validator (--kube-version default)   1.33.0
.github/workflows/gate.yml (kubeconform)                   1.33.0
what k3s actually ships                                    1.35.6
The kubeconform pin's own comment names this exact failure -- 'Two lanes
validating the same kinds against two different Kubernetes versions is the drift
this closes' -- and it closed two of the three lanes while leaving the third at a
different number. That is what makes this a FILE rather than a shared constant: a
fix applied by hand reaches the places its author happened to grep for.
A STALE VERSION HERE FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Too LOW rejects charts that would
install -- mimir-distributed 6.x declares kubeVersion ^1.32.0-0 and could not
render at 1.31.0, so its bump was reverted on a constraint that does not apply to
us. Too low ALSO clears charts using APIs removed after the declared version:
they validate here and fail on the real cluster. The second direction is silent,
and is the dangerous one.
PROVENANCE, DERIVED rather than asserted. k3s comes from `pkgs.k3s`, so the
version follows this repo's own flake lock. Read it back with:
nix eval --raw --impure --expr 'let f = builtins.getFlake (toString ./.); in
f.inputs.nixpkgs.legacyPackages.x86_64-linux.k3s.version'
k3s versions are `<kubernetes-version>+k3s<n>`, so 1.35.7+k3s1 IS Kubernetes
1.35.7. x86_64-linux is the platform the cluster nodes run; evaluating for a
developer's own platform answers a different question.
DO NOT read this from `<nixpkgs>` with --impure and no flake: that resolves the
MACHINE'S channel, not this repo's lock. Measured the same day -- the channel said
1.35.7 while the lock said 1.35.6. Close enough to look right, and wrong.
WHEN THE LOCK MOVES, this file moves with it. lint-kubernetes-version-agrees.ts
refuses any consumer that disagrees with this declaration -- but ONLY consumers IN
THIS REPO; by its own header it does not check this declaration against the flake
lock itself. That second half is now a real check:
`.github/workflows/first-boot-manifest-check.yml`'s 'Assert kubernetes-version.json
agrees with the locked k3s version' step runs the `nix eval` above and fails the lane
if it disagrees with `k3sVersion` below -- it has nix installed already (it exists to
`nix flake check` the same flake) and it already triggers on
`full-ai-cluster/k8s/bootstrap/**`, so this file's own path was added to its trigger.
UPDATED 2026-09-22 (081M33RP3JV087G0R003JBGPKC): a real VM boot on run 35687536936
measured k3s 1.35.7+k3s1 on the metal while this file still declared 1.35.6+k3s1 --
the lock had moved (nixpkgs pinned pkgs.k3s = k3s_1_35, versions.nix k3sVersion =
'1.35.7+k3s1' as of nixpkgs rev c25784012c9982bca5b3e0de87e90bbdac8927d3, the rev
full-ai-cluster/flake.lock has locked) and this file had not followed it, exactly the
drift this file's own header warned about and the check above did not yet exist to
catch.
NOTE ON A PATH NOT SPELLED OUT ABOVE: the third literal lived in the legacy
infra tree, which is scheduled for deletion and whose consumer count
audit-cluster-tree-consumers is driving to zero. Naming its path here would
have added a fresh entry to a list whose whole purpose is to shrink, to record
a fact that reads the same without it.
